provenance.functions: Expected values computed by running Factory v2's TypeScript (origin/main 2fa0e461a4ba: same-person.ts, device-repeat.ts, ip-reputation.ts, email.ts, email-validation.ts) under Node 26 type stripping, with v2's stubDnsResolver semantics for email_flags and email_gate.
provenance.scenarios: Expected decisions derived from register.ts, oauth.ts, device-repeat.ts, same-person.ts and referrals/signup.ts. Factory v2's parity test runs the same scenarios through assessSignup.
provenance.data: Synthetic: example addresses and test IPs only. Reasons name accounts by their scenario id; Factory names the earlier account by email (same_device:<email>), so compare kinds, not details.

conventions.time: Scenario steps run in order at their 'at' time (occurred_at). Windows are [at - window, at).
conventions.check: Each check step evaluates the signup (POST /api/v2/check, mode evaluate) and, unless it is blocked, commits it as request.account.id (POST /api/v2/accounts): like v2, a refused signup creates no account. expect lists the exact hard and soft reason codes in order (weak reasons are Guardpost-only), the decision, the actions, the block code and the referral verdict (null when the request has no referral).
conventions.ip_reputation: Rows merged into the shared IP reputation table (Factory v2 ip_reputation columns).
conventions.dns: MX table for the scenario (unknown names: no MX); trusted domains never reach DNS.
conventions.tenant: A fresh instance per scenario (empty ledger and shared IP reputation), one tenant with the default config.
conventions.trusted_extra_domains: email_flags and email_gate run with the Factory tenant's extra trusted domains (factory.bot, deleted.local), which v2 keeps in its shared list.

known_divergences.description: Guardpost canonicalizes an address (RFC 5952 IPv6, IPv4-mapped/compatible hex forms) before keying it; v2 compares the raw strings. The same address written two ways matches in Guardpost only. Factory receives canonical addresses from its proxy, so this is latent.

Guardpost's typo gate also matches its mistyped-TLD rule (typo_domain:tld, e.g. hotmail.con) and its own extra map entries. v2 sends such an address to the MX gate, where it usually fails as EMAIL_DOMAIN_UNDELIVERABLE (block_mismatch on the code only).

homograph_domain, null_mx, role_account_extended, gibberish_domain and relay_domain exist only in Guardpost. They are weak (score only) and never change the decision, but they appear in reasons (reasons_differ).
Guardpost's disposable domains, MX hosts, keywords and typo map are a superset of Factory's (tests/test_factory_superset.py): a Guardpost-only entry flags an address v2 passes (gp_stricter).
Guardpost cannot recognise a returning user (a deleted account's email key is nulled); it trusts signup.returning_user from the app.
v2 resolves the referral code itself (unknown and promo codes, retracted codes); Guardpost receives referrer_account_id and knows a retraction only through referral_code_retracted events.

In commit (shadow) mode Guardpost records an account it would have blocked, because the app created it, and counts it as suspicious on the shared IP counters; v2 writes nothing for a refused signup. Only reachable when the decisions already differ.

Guardpost bounds every lookup by occurred_at (windows [t - w, t), alias collisions with accounts created before t), so a replay sees the ledger as it was. v2 reads the live table at wall-clock time; identical for real-time signups.
v2 caches MX answers for 6 h; Guardpost's v2 check asks its resolver every time (the default dnspython path caches for the process lifetime).

Factory emits graylisted_ip:<status reason> and blacklisted_ip:<status reason> (e.g. graylisted_ip:5 suspicious registrations). The shared reputation's counts include every tenant's signups, so Guardpost emits the status only (graylisted_ip:graylisted, blacklisted_ip:blacklisted) and no ip_reason/subnet_reason, unless the tenant sets ip.reason_detail = full and is alone on the instance (or the operator allows it). Compare these two reasons on the kind. subnet_burst:<cidr> is unchanged: the /24 is the caller's own.
